investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had insufficient remaining capacity (resource exhaustion), and 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-bearing nodes. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~148 seconds before the eval timed out, the agent VM was never created, and the runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885, createAgent call) never received a response from which to populate the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots on the peer-pod-capable nodes are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's node affinity/selector rules exclude 4 of 6 nodes from consideration entirely, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes. If those rules are overly restrictive or if node labels changed, the effective scheduling pool shrinks to zero when the 2 nodes are full.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes (2) may be insufficient for the concurrent demand from the eval suite plus any live workloads, with no headroom for new pods.

Quaternary — preemption policy prevents recovery: the scheduler reports 'No preemption victims found' on both resource-bearing nodes, meaning no lower-priority pods can be evicted to free capacity. This could indicate all running pods on those nodes have equal or higher priority than the incoming remote-agent pod.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Blocks All Remote-Agent Evals
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent evals (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-25T11:18–11:23Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the requested kata peer-pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the remote-agent-state expected-output contract was fully violated.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota across the two eligible nodes, and the remaining four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every eval pod was stuck Unschedulable for ~145–148 s before the eval runner timed out. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct and accurate reflection of the underlying scheduling failure; no evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present in the packet, so impact is scoped to the observability eval layer.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had insufficient remaining capacity (resource exhaustion), and 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-bearing nodes. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~148 seconds before the eval timed out, the agent VM was never created, and the runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885, createAgent call) never received a response from which to populate the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots on the peer-pod-capable nodes are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's node affinity/selector rules exclude 4 of 6 nodes from consideration entirely, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes. If those rules are overly restrictive or if node labels changed, the effective scheduling pool shrinks to zero when the 2 nodes are full.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes (2) may be insufficient for the concurrent demand from the eval suite plus any live workloads, with no headroom for new pods.

Quaternary — preemption policy prevents recovery: the scheduler reports 'No preemption victims found' on both resource-bearing nodes, meaning no lower-priority pods can be evicted to free capacity. This could indicate all running pods on those nodes have equal or higher priority than the incoming remote-agent pod.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm slots available (allocatable > requested), the resource exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and the cause would shift to a scheduler bug, admission webhook rejection, or pod spec error.

If a new eval run succeeds immediately without any cluster changes, it would suggest the failure was transient (e.g., a briefly saturated node that freed up) rather than a persistent capacity shortage.

If the 4 nodes that did not match affinity/selector are shown to have available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the affinity/selector is found to be misconfigured (e.g., wrong label key/value), the root cause would shift from capacity exhaustion to affinity misconfiguration.

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed in a subsequent run, it would indicate the failure is isolated to the runtime probe rather than a cluster-wide scheduling problem.
If no kata.peerpods.io/vm resource type exists on any node in the cluster, the cause would be a missing resource registration rather than exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add an eval or verifier probe that directly checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on affinity-eligible nodes before attempting to create a remote agent pod, so capacity exhaustion is detected and reported as a distinct infrastructure signal rather than a pod scheduling timeout.
Add a pre-flight check eval that validates node affinity/selector label presence on cluster nodes, alerting when the count of eligible nodes drops below a configured threshold (e.g., below 3).

Add a stale-pod detection eval that identifies remote-agent pods stuck in Pending/Unschedulable state for longer than a configurable threshold and reports them as a separate check, distinct from the agent creation and runtime checks.
Consider a synthetic eval that measures kata.peerpods.io/vm slot utilization as a percentage and warns before full exhaustion, providing earlier signal than a scheduling failure.
